subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Should this PR become the single canonical fix for the exec-approvals VirtioFS lock leak instead of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 after it supplies exact-head live proof?
rationale: Both open PRs modify the same security-sensitive lock boundary and claim the same root-cause fix; source-level tests alone cannot select a permanent implementation or prove the reported mount-specific release behavior.

options.title: Select this hardened branch after proof
options.body: Require redacted current-head VirtioFS output showing lock removal and a subsequent configured-policy read, then land this branch as the sole canonical fix.

options.title: Select the earlier async-lock PR
options.body: Adopt https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 instead if maintainers prefer its implementation and can obtain equally current, inspectable proof.

options.title: Pause local replacement for shared design
options.body: Defer both PRs while deciding whether the long-term fix belongs in a separately reviewed `@openclaw/fs-safe` release.

recommendation.title: Select this hardened branch after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted current-head VirtioFS output showing lock removal and a subsequent configured-policy read, then land this branch as the sole canonical fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Their production reproduction and overlapping implementation provide the strongest available context for comparing the two candidate designs.
